report:
Source assessment: The complete claim requires stable rule pages, definition and context, all implementation and test evidence with Rust excerpts and surrounding-source access, and independently inspectable placeholder statuses and explanations. The ordinary anchors.rs association satisfies the presentation behavior: children enumerates dotted namespaces and every rule; anchor_url maps names deterministically; page renders the complete claim and context, loops over all implementation sites and tests, emits separate evidence sections, statuses, implementation explanations, complete test bodies (including their rationale comments), and source links. No collection is collapsed into a single badge. Missing associations are visibly errors. The changed test-source lookup matches file plus crate/target/Rust-path selector; captured inventory code constructs exactly these fragments and rejects ambiguous test identities. Review rendering now distinguishes accepted, changes-requested, unfinished and pending records without changing per-entry statuses.

Complete test set: generated_anchor_pages_join_namespaces_claims_implementations_tests_and_reviews constructs ordinary, TODO and N/A evidence across parent/child/sibling rules and checks stable generated paths, retained parent-as-namespace children, definition/context navigation, literal implementation and test excerpts, source access, TODO/N/A explanations and badges, and exclusion of generated copies from definitions. Its updated assertions also cover accepted, requested-edit and unfinished review displays, plus escaped multiline report text. Captured fixture and chapters helpers establish that these assertions inspect actual preprocessor output. canonical_anchor_pages is explicitly TODO for exhaustive stable-page/all-site/excerpt/status/explanation verification; completing that matrix of presentation assertions is its remaining prerequisite. It is a documented coverage deferral, not implemented test evidence. Existing integration assertions plus source inspection substantiate current behavior while leaving that broader coverage visibly deferred.

Baseline comparison: independently compared historical source snapshots to current files; spec_plan.rs is an exact byte match. anchors.rs and book.rs differ; inspected their complete relevant current behavior and deltas (fragment-based excerpt retrieval, new recorded-output display and fixture/assertions). Historical rationale remains sufficient for unchanged presentation behavior, with the above reassessment replacing obsolete review-output details. Additional inventory, URL and fixture dependencies were captured through review read.

Execution: personally ran review start and review read, source comparisons and inspection; no behavioral tests or build were rerun. The coordinator reports 321 functional sage-meta tests and root cargo build passing; that is separate baseline execution, not my execution. No source edits or unresolved behavioral concerns were identified.
